Overstated wording, abstract and A4 section: 'the pooled format also chose the right one more often (+0.18)'. That gain is mostly a definitional artifact of the ISO hit (right accepted AND both wrong rejected). The single-call isolated accept rate of the right candidate on UNSOLVED TP pools is 0.628 (n=78), equal to PICK's hit 0.615. Against EACH, which uses the same pool context, the hit gain is +0.05 [-0.05,+0.16], not detectable. So the 'hits rose with false choices, consistent with a criterion shift' reading rests on an asymmetric pre-specified definition (strict hit, any-of-three false choice, three ISO calls vs one PICK call), and the rule written in A4 hard-wires that reading. Suggest saying 'higher than strict-ISO hit rate; not detectably higher than EACH or single-call ISO acceptance'. The H7 null (stating most problems have no solution did not move the criterion) also cuts against a pure criterion-shift mechanism and deserves the same prominence.

Headline framing versus the primary test. C3 was preregistered to test whether the penalty depends on solvability; H1 (interaction) is inconclusive for haiku (b=+0.12, one-sided p 0.065, Holm 0.129) and null for sonnet (b=-0.02). SOLVED d=+0.06 [+0.01,+0.11] is also above zero. The title and first abstract sentences speak of 'problems it did not solve', which invites a solvability-specific reading the data do not establish. The abstract does report H1 as inconclusive, but last; the strata are defined by haiku, so for sonnet they are 'haiku-unsolved'. Power: preregistration expected SE(b)~0.064 and detectable effect ~0.16 with ~100 per stratum; achieved SE 0.078 on 90/137, so H1 was underpowered for a +0.12 effect, which the paper should say.

Mislabeled strata and candidates: 20 of 90 UNSOLVED problems (22%) were found post hoc to be grader errors (14 solved, 6 mixed), and 6 pools had mislabelled-correct or garbled 'wrong' candidates. Both are disclosed and robust in sensitivity (above), but the preregistered strata remain the confirmatory ones, so say that 'UNSOLVED' is a noisy label. The A1 text claims all 22 grader disagreements were equivalent forms; the later audit shows both graders missed more equivalences.

A4 and A5 are described as pre-registered; timestamps are consistent (A4 commit 10:09:20 before first A4 raw 10:10; A5 10:53:58 before first A5 raw 10:54) but both were designed after the C3 results and in response to review. 'Pre-registered after seeing C3 results' is the accurate phrase. H4 and H6 rest on a single pass over the same 227 problems; the A5 ROC has only five points and both curves are near chance on UNSOLVED (pick hit 0.60, fa 0.67 at t=1), so the null is uninformative, as the paper itself says.

Compute asymmetry: d compares one PICK call with any acceptance across three ISO calls. That is disclosed, and it works against the finding (ISO-any is inflated), so the +0.24 is conservative. A matched comparison to EACH (+0.13 [+0.01,+0.25], estimated only) is the cleaner presentation-versus-form contrast and is weaker.
